title: Bill Ackman, George Soros and 5 Other Famous Investors Own Microsoft. Here’s Who Bought and Sold Recently

Bill Ackman, George Soros and 5 Other Famous Investors Own Microsoft. Here's Who Bought and Sold Recently ©Natee Meepian's Images and Mike Marchetti from baseimage via Canva
Key Takeaways

Seven famous investors held Microsoft on Sept. 30. Dan Loeb's Third Point and Peter Thiel's Thiel Macro opened new stakes, while Bill Ackman's Pershing Square and George Soros' fund each cut about a third of theirs.

AI spending has cut into Microsoft's cash, and analysts expect $32.0 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2027, down from $67.0 billion in fiscal 2026. Amazon's spending has already turned its free cash flow negative.

Analysts expect earnings per share to grow 16% in fiscal 2027 and 21% in fiscal 2028, and the stock trades at 24x forward earnings, against a five-year average of 29x.

The numbers side with the buyers. The December-quarter report in late January will show whether the cash holds up.

Seven famous investors held Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) at the end of September, according to their 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed from Nov. 6 to Nov. 16. They didn't agree on it: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square and George Soros' Soros Fund Management cut their stakes, while Dan Loeb's Third Point and Peter Thiel's Thiel Macro bought in.

The split comes as Microsoft's AI build-out eats into its cash. Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) has the same problem, and its free cash flow has already gone negative.

Ackman and Soros sold, Loeb and Thiel bought

The biggest move in dollars was a sale. Pershing Square cut its stake 35% in the third quarter, to 4.06 million shares from 6.21 million, which is about $1.10 billion of stock at quarter-end prices. Even after the cut, Microsoft was still Pershing's fourth-largest holding at $2.08 billion, or 6.8% of its 13F stocks. Soros Fund Management cut 36%, to 122,166 shares, and what's left is 1.0% of its 13F stocks.

On the buying side, Third Point opened a 450,000-share stake worth $231 million. That made Microsoft its sixth-largest holding, at 5.1% of its 13F stocks. Thiel Macro's new stake is a token one: 2,000 shares worth about $1 million, or 0.2% of the $460 million its 13F holds in US stocks.

Everyone else mostly held on

The other three holders barely moved. Ken Fisher's Fisher Investments is by far the biggest of the seven, with 27.14 million shares worth $13.92 billion on Sept. 30 after adding 2%. Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital trimmed 7% and still held $607 million, its eighth-largest position. Cathie Wood's ARK Invest cut 8%, to just 5,693 shares. Microsoft stock is down 3% from its quarter-end price, so it has barely moved since the filings' snapshot.
